input.content:
Every document carries a `PHAuthState` with `version: 0` until something initializes it. In that state the policy is **uninitialized** and the decision model allows everything — which is exactly what keeps the fleet's existing documents unaffected when enforcement turns on: nothing in production has ever emitted `INITIALIZE_AUTH`, so every existing document is open.

`INITIALIZE_AUTH` installs the first grant list and is genesis-only. From then on the default is **deny**: if no grant applies to a request, it is refused with `deniedReason: "no grant permits this operation"`. The `document-acl` recipe's demo makes the flip visible — Bob writes freely before any policy exists, then Alice initializes a three-grant policy and Bob's `SET_TITLE` / `PIN_ENTRY` / `SET_GRANT` are refused while the `{anyone}` grant on `ADD_ENTRY` still lets his entries land.

The open default is also a trap for hosts that think the other way round. Hosts exist whose own access control closes a document until something opens it; for them "no policy" has always meant closed. The spec lets such a host configure its **read surface** to withhold every gated scope of an uninitialized document — a host-local second system that is safe only because it never widens: it withholds, and a read decision is never part of any document's history.

On acceptance of the genesis, the signer's key is stored as `creator` in the auth state and the header is consulted only at that one binding.
